issues.legal_issue: Members of an unlawful assembly are vicariously liable for murders committed in pursuit of its common object or which they knew were likely to be committed in pursuit of that object.
material_facts: An armed group of more than twenty people went to enforce control over the distribution of water by criminal force.
The group opened fire after members of the opposing party objected, killing four people and injuring another, who was later killed.
The victims’ bodies were dragged, dismembered and burned, and some members carried away severed heads.

The High Court found that the accused party had gone to the field armed to enforce its object by force and that those who took part in the incident also took part in moving the bodies and attempting to destroy evidence.
Five respondents whose participation in the assembly and the incident was established had been convicted of destroying evidence, but their murder convictions had been set aside.
issues.conclusion: The assembly was unlawful, and the five respondents were liable under section 302 read with section 149 of the Indian Penal Code for the five murders; their murder convictions were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 141, fourth paragraph, of the Indian Penal Code, an assembly of five or more persons is unlawful when its common object is to deprive a person of the use of water or to enforce a right or supposed right by criminal force; under the Explanation to section 141, an assembly may become unlawful after it assembles. Under section 149, every member is liable for an offence committed in prosecution of the assembly’s common object, and liability also extends to an offence the members knew was likely to be committed in prosecution of that object. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: state_appeal_after_murder_acquittals and assembly_gathered_to_enforce_right_by_criminal_force and accused_membership_established and (murders_pursued_common_object or members_knew_murders_likely) and accused_participated_in_incident

predicates.state_appeal_after_murder_acquittals: The State appealed after a court had set aside murder convictions for some accused.
predicates.assembly_gathered_to_enforce_right_by_cr: An assembly gathered to enforce a right or supposed right by using criminal force.
predicates.accused_membership_established: The accused’s membership in the assembly was established.
predicates.murders_pursued_common_object: The murders were committed in pursuit of the assembly’s common object.
predicates.members_knew_murders_likely: The assembly members knew that murders were likely to be committed in pursuit of the assembly’s common object.
predicates.accused_participated_in_incident: The accused took part in the incident, including its initial or later stages.

issues.definition: When a State appeal follows murder acquittals, established membership in an assembly gathered to enforce a right by criminal force, together with participation in the incident and either pursuit of the common object through murder or knowledge that murder was likely, results in vicarious liability for the murders.

issues.legal_issue: The sentence for a participant’s murder liability may reflect the participant’s prominence and active role in achieving the assembly’s common object.
material_facts: Three respondents were shown to have been armed with chopping weapons and to have decapitated the victims, severed their limbs and thrown the dismembered bodies into a fire.
The Court considered these respondents prominent members whose active participation was necessary for the assembly to achieve its common object.
The trial court had imposed death sentences, which the High Court had displaced when it set aside their murder convictions.
issues.conclusion: The death sentences imposed on the three prominent participants were restored, along with their concurrent sentences for other offences.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 302 read with section 149 of the Indian Penal Code and distinguished sentence according to the respondents’ proved roles: the three participants’ prominent and active involvement in achieving the assembly’s common object warranted restoration of the trial court’s death sentences. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_reviewing_sentence and vicarious_murder_liability_established and prominent_participant and actively_helped_achieve_common_object

predicates.criminal_appeal_reviewing_sentence: A criminal appeal asked the court to review a sentence imposed for murder liability.
predicates.vicarious_murder_liability_established: The accused’s vicarious liability for murder was established.
predicates.prominent_participant: The accused was a prominent member of the assembly.
predicates.actively_helped_achieve_common_object: The accused actively helped the assembly achieve its common object.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal reviewing sentence, when murder liability is established and the accused was a prominent member whose active participation helped achieve the assembly’s common object, the death sentence is restored.

issues.legal_issue: A lesser sentence is appropriate for a member whose murder liability is established but whose arming and role are not clearly shown.
material_facts: Two respondents were found to be members of the unlawful assembly and were liable for the murders.
The evidence did not clearly show how either respondent was armed, or whether either was armed at all.
The trial court had imposed life sentences on these respondents.
issues.conclusion: The life sentences imposed on the two respondents were confirmed, along with their concurrent sentences for other offences.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 302 read with section 149 of the Indian Penal Code and treated the uncertainty about the respondents’ arming and individual roles as supporting the lesser sentence rather than the death sentence. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.criminal_appeal_reviewing_sentence: A criminal appeal asked the court to review a sentence imposed for murder liability.
predicates.vicarious_murder_liability_established: The accused’s vicarious liability for murder was established.
predicates.evidence_unclear_whether_accused_was_arm: The evidence did not clearly establish how the accused was armed or whether the accused was armed.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal reviews a sentence for established vicarious murder liability and the evidence does not clearly show whether the accused was armed, the life sentence is confirmed.

issues.legal_issue: An acquittal should not be reversed merely because another view of the evidence is possible when the acquittal finding is not perverse or against the weight of the evidence.
material_facts: The High Court acquitted three respondents after expressing doubt about their presence and the acts attributed to them.
The eyewitnesses may not have been positioned to see whether those respondents arrived with the group or were armed.
The Supreme Court considered that another view of the evidence might be possible but found that the High Court’s finding was not perverse or against the weight of the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The acquittals of the three respondents were confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: In a State appeal against acquittal, the possibility of taking a different view of the evidence is not by itself enough to interfere with the acquittal where the finding is not perverse or against the weight of the evidence. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this principle in the judgment.

predicates.state_appeal_against_acquittal: The State appealed against an accused’s acquittal.
predicates.evidence_about_accused_presence_or_role_: The evidence did not clearly establish the accused’s presence or the acts attributed to the accused.
predicates.acquittal_finding_not_perverse_or_agains: The appellate court’s acquittal finding was neither perverse nor against the weight of the evidence.

issues.definition: In a State appeal against acquittal, when evidence about the accused’s presence or role is uncertain and the acquittal finding is not perverse or against the weight of the evidence, the acquittal remains undisturbed.
